_comment: EXAMPLE of data/backfill/state.json -- backfill.py's resumable cursor.
Illustrative invented numbers, from a hypothetical ~40k-row export.
DO NOT COPY THIS TO state.json. backfill.py creates the real file itself on
its first run; copying this one would fast-forward the cursor past 5,000
unprocessed rows. This exists only so a stalled sweep can be diagnosed.
next_row  the CSV row the next run resumes from. Advanced only at a
checkpoint (every 50 rows) and always AFTER the manifest is saved,
so a crash re-does work rather than losing it. --offset overrides
it for one run without moving it; --retry-failed never touches it.
totals    cumulative outcome counts across every run, not just the last one.
They are per-IMAGE, while `processed` is per-ROW, so on an export
with galleries in it the buckets legitimately sum to MORE than
hash_bits the pHash depth of the index this sweep was calibrated against.
Recorded so a later run against a differently-built index is
detectable -- distances across depths are meaningless.
updated_at UTC, rewritten at every checkpoint. If this stops advancing while
a sweep appears to be running, the sweep is wedged, not working.
